It solves the problem of information loss in deep volumetric networks by enabling the decoder to access high-resolution features from the encoder, making it dominant for volume super-resolution and segmentation where local receptive fields match volumetric spatial locality [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the architecture (U-Net) solves information loss by enabling the decoder to access high-resolution features from the encoder via skip connections, and that it is dominant for volume super-resolution and segmentation because local receptive fields match volumetric spatial locality. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states: 'The U-Net variant [118] adds skip connections between corresponding encoder and decoder stages.' It further states: '3D CNNs and U-Net are the dominant architectures for volume SR (Sec. 3) and segmentation (Sec. 6), where their local receptive fields naturally match the spatial locality of volumetric features.' While the specific phrase 'solves the problem of information loss' is a standard interpretation of why skip connections are used in U-Net (and implied by the context of 'reconstructing spatial features'), the core factual assertions regarding the mechanism (skip connections), the dominance in specific tasks, and the reason (matching spatial locality) are directly present in the text.
supported

VC-Net is a network for microvascular segmentation in cerebrovascular micro-MRI that combines 3D U-Net on raw volumes with 2D U-Net on Maximum Intensity Projections (MIPs), fusing them via a volume-composition module [S1, unofficial].

The claim accurately reflects the information provided in Source [S1]. The source explicitly states that 'VC-Net combines a 3D U-Net operating on the raw volume with a 2D U-Net operating on maximum intensity projections (MIPs)' and that 'A volume-composition module fuses the two streams by projecting 2D contextual predictions back into 3D space.' It also confirms the context of 'microvascular segmentation in cerebrovascular micro-MRI'.
